analysis.one_liner: Bank of Baroda is a government-owned (PSU) commercial bank that takes deposits and lends to retail, agriculture, MSME and corporate customers across India and roughly 17 other countries.
analysis.whats_happening: NMC Healthcare founder B.R. Shetty has filed a fresh $15 billion damages suit against Bank of Baroda and 25 others in mid-October 2026, alleging collusion in the NMC fraud — this comes just months after BoB itself paid $600 million (about Rs 5,680 crore) to settle separate claims from NMC entities in July 2026, without admitting liability. BoB says it will contest the new claim. The stock hit a fresh 52-week low (₹227.5) this week, pressured by this legal overhang plus broad PSU-bank weakness. A Q2 FY27 (September quarter) business update filed on 3 October 2026 showed healthy advances and deposit growth, but full profit and asset-quality numbers for that quarter were not yet out as of this writing.
analysis.plain_terms: This is India's government-owned bank, so when you buy the stock you are betting on how well a large, old-style lender manages growth, bad loans and legal risk. The headline profit number for the June 2026 quarter looked terrible — down 72% — but that was a one-off legal payout, not the bank suddenly lending badly. The tension to watch: the underlying business (loans, deposits, bad-loan ratios) looks fine and is growing, but a fresh, very large lawsuit from a UAE businessman means the legal story isn't over, and the market is pricing in more uncertainty than the loan book alone would suggest.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (June 2026) reported net profit of just Rs 1,278 crore, down 72% year-on-year — but this reflects a one-time Rs 5,680 crore outflow tied to the NMC Healthcare legal settlement, not business weakness. Strip that out and underlying profit would have been around Rs 5,528 crore. Core metrics were healthy: net interest income rose 9.5% to Rs 12,524 crore, operating profit was Rs 8,127 crore, and both GNPA (1.99%) and NNPA (0.50%) improved year-on-year. Margins were flat — domestic NIM 2.93%, global NIM 2.77%. The Q2 FY27 (September 2026 quarter) business update (filed 3 October 2026) showed global advances up 18.27% YoY and deposits up 16.75%, but the full profit-and-loss and asset-quality figures for that quarter had not been published as of 17 October 2026 — treat any profit number for this quarter as unverified until the results are out.
analysis.performance_read: Over 5 years the stock is up 188% versus the Nifty's 25% — but that mostly reflects a low-base recovery from the PSU bank bad-loan crisis of 2020-21, not steady compounding. More recent numbers are weaker: over 1 year the stock is down 10.6% (similar to the Nifty's -9.5%, but behind peer PNB's +3.1%), and over 3 years it is up only 22% against PNB's 64% — BoB has clearly lagged its direct peer on a multi-year view even though the longer 5-year number still looks strong. The stock is down 26.7% from its February 2026 peak of ₹314.28 and is currently at a fresh 52-week low (₹227.5). The 2015 stock split (5-for-1) is already reflected in these adjusted figures and is not a factor in the current fall.
analysis.valuation_read: At roughly 6.5–6.7x trailing earnings and about 0.71–0.77x book value, BoB trades well below private banks (HDFC Bank near 14x, ICICI near 17x, Kotak near 20x earnings) and even below SBI's ~10.5x. Why it's cheap: PSU banks carry a structural discount tied to government ownership, lower capital efficiency, and periodic contingent liabilities like the current NMC/Shetty legal matter. Whether that discount is too deep is a separate question — it depends on whether the bank's ~12% ROE holds up and whether the legal overhang stays contained rather than escalating.
analysis.growth_read: Growth here is volume-led, not margin-led. Global advances grew 16–18% through FY26 and into Q2 FY27, with the international book (+24% in FY26) outgrowing the domestic one (+14.5%). Margins are flat to mildly thin — domestic NIM 2.93%, global NIM 2.77% — so profit growth depends on the balance sheet continuing to expand rather than on better pricing. Within domestic lending, retail (+17.9%), agriculture (+20.7%) and MSME (+15.6%) are leading growth.
analysis.health_read: Asset quality has genuinely improved: GNPA is down to 1.99% (1.89% at FY26 year-end) and NNPA is a low 0.50%, both better than a year ago — the legacy PSU bad-loan problem looks largely behind the bank. The live risk now is not balance-sheet credit risk but legal/contingent liability: the NMC Healthcare matter already cost Rs 5,680 crore in cash this year, and a fresh $15 billion claim from B.R. Shetty is unresolved. Capital adequacy has also thinned — CRAR fell to 15.82% from 17.19% a year earlier — worth watching if loan growth keeps running at mid-teens pace.
analysis.ownership_read: The Government of India is the promoter at 63.97%, unchanged quarter-on-quarter, with zero pledging. Domestic mutual funds hold 9.49% and total DIIs 17.91%, while foreign institutional ownership is unusually thin at just 0.81% for a bank this size — suggesting foreign investors have largely stayed away. Not verified - check on Screener for any specific marquee individual investor; none turned up in the sources checked, and none appears to be on the register.
strengths: GNPA at 1.99% and NNPA at 0.50%, both improved year-on-year — the PSU bad-loan overhang has largely receded
Loan book growing 16-18% YoY through FY26 and into Q2 FY27, with retail (+17.9%) and agri (+20.7%) leading domestic growth
Valuation of ~0.73x book and ~6.6x earnings is cheap relative to private-bank peers, leaving room for re-rating if execution stays clean
Zero promoter pledging and a stable government promoter base (63.97%)
watchpoints: A fresh $15 billion lawsuit from B.R. Shetty (October 2026) keeps the legal overhang alive even after the Rs 5,680 crore NMC settlement already paid in July 2026
Capital adequacy (CRAR) slipped to 15.82% from 17.19% a year earlier — worth tracking if loan growth keeps running at mid-teens pace
Margins are flat-to-thin (domestic NIM 2.93%), so profit growth leans entirely on continued double-digit loan growth rather than pricing power
Stock is at a fresh 52-week low, down 26.7% from its February 2026 peak, and has trailed peer PNB over both the 1-year and 3-year horizons
analysis.one_thing: How the Shetty $15 billion claim is treated by courts/regulators in the coming months — containment would remove the main overhang on the stock, while escalation could mean provisioning beyond the Rs 5,680 crore already paid.
analysis.data_notes: Cross-checked Q1 FY27 and FY26 results across ICICI Direct, PSU Connect, Multibagg and IndianMasterminds, and the NMC settlement/lawsuit facts across Free Press Journal, Gulf News, Deccan Herald and The National. Valuation multiples (P/E 6.45-6.74x, P/B 0.71-0.77x, ROE 11.9-12.5%) vary slightly across sources/dates; the cluster of figures was used and the range flagged rather than averaged. Full Q2 FY27 (September 2026 quarter) profit and asset-quality figures were not yet published as of 17 October 2026 — only the advances/deposits business update (filed 3 October 2026) was available; exact results date not independently confirmed - check Screener or BSE filings.
